request: Independent full-visible-text coherence review of the retained GLM DCP1 natural long-output case; inspect off-topic drift, token/sentence degeneration, chapter completeness, and cross-chapter coherence without executing generated code or treating static application correctness as the gate.

findings_summary.finding: No off-topic drift or late-output collapse was found. All 24 chapters stay within the deterministic Python platformer-engine assignment, remain distinct, and preserve the fixed-point/tick/state-layer design through the final chapter.

No repeated-token, repeated-sentence, repeated-paragraph, or long-window degeneration was found. Offline probes found no duplicate normalized sentence of at least 8 words, no duplicate paragraph of at least 20 words, no duplicate 30-word window, and a maximum identical-token run of 2.

Chapter coverage is complete: exact ordered headings 01 through 24, every chapter contains substantive topic-specific explanation, at least one concrete code block, an Invariants section, and a Failure cases section; the exact terminal marker occurs once at EOF.

Length undershoots the aspirational wording: 11,069 visible words is 92.2% of the 12,000-word aim; 22 of 24 chapter bodies are below 500 words and 5 are below 400 when code is counted. The shortest is 357 words. Because the prompt says approximately and every chapter remains developed rather than collapsing late, this is an instruction-completeness limitation, not a coherence failure.

The prose is coherent, but it is not an integrated implementation acceptance. Static seams remain, including the slope chapter requiring insertion between X/Y while the prior example exposes a combined move_and_collide function, and the save chapter claiming complete reconstruction while its example omits some dynamic counters and treats stateful platforms as tick-derived. Generated code was not executed.
